Because that letter was written on the same damaged typewriter that the other letters were written on and those gangsters have not failed to make any of their threats good."

arxiv-2011-13671.title: A combinatorial Schur expansion of triangle-free horizontal-strip LLT polynomials Thanks: The author was supported in part by the National Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada.
arxiv-2011-13671.creator: Foster Tom
arxiv-2011-13671.description: Abstract . In recent years, Alexandersson and others proved combinatorial formulas for the Schur function expansion of the horizontal-strip LLT polynomial G 𝝀 ​ ( 𝒙 , q ) G_{\bm{\lambda}}(\bm{x};q) in some special cases. We associate a weighted graph Π \Pi to 𝝀 \bm{\lambda} and we use it to express a linear relation among LLT polynomials.

arxiv-2012-01077.title: Roots of Gårding hyperbolic polynomials Thanks: The author was supported by the Austrian Science Fund (FWF), START Programme Y963 and P 32905-N
arxiv-2012-01077.creator: Armin Rainer
arxiv-2012-01077.description: Abstract . We explore the regularity of the roots of Gårding hyperbolic polynomials and real stable polynomials. As an application we obtain new regularity results of Sobolev type for the eigenvalues of Hermitian matrices and for the singular values of arbitrary matrices. These results are optimal among all Sobolev spaces. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 26C05, 15A18, 32A08, 46E35, 1.

arxiv-2107-00316.title: Leveraging Domain Agnostic and Specific Knowledge for Acronym Disambiguation
arxiv-2107-00316.creator: Qiwei Zhong, Guanxiong Zeng, Danqing Zhu, Yang Zhang, Wangli Lin, Ben Chen, Jiayu Tang
arxiv-2107-00316.description: Abstract An obstacle to scientific document understanding is the extensive use of acronyms which are shortened forms of long technical phrases. Acronym disambiguation aims to find the correct meaning of an ambiguous acronym in a given text. Recent efforts attempted to incorporate word embeddings and deep learning architectures, and achieved significant effects in this task.

arxiv-2210-08423.title: TransVisDrone: Spatio-Temporal Trans former for Vis ion-based Drone -to-Drone Detection in Aerial Videos
arxiv-2210-08423.creator: Tushar Sangam, Ishan Rajendrakumar Dave, Waqas Sultani, Mubarak Shah
arxiv-2210-08423.description: Abstract Drone-to-drone detection using visual feed has crucial applications, such as detecting drone collisions, detecting drone attacks, or coordinating flight with other drones. However, existing methods are computationally costly, follow non-end-to-end optimization, and have complex multi-stage pipelines, making them less suitable for real-time deployment on edge devices.

arxiv-2306-07800.title: Poisson derivations of a semiclassical limit of a family of quantum second Weyl algebras
arxiv-2306-07800.creator: S Launois and I Oppong
arxiv-2306-07800.description: Abstract In [ 15 ] , we studied deformations A α , β A_{\alpha,\beta} of the second Weyl algebra and computed their derivations. In the present paper, we identify the semiclassical limits 𝒜 α , β \mathcal{A}_{\alpha,\beta} of these deformations and compute their Poisson derivations.

arxiv-2401-15968.title: Imitation vs Serendipity in Ranking Dynamics
arxiv-2401-15968.creator: Federica De Domenico, Fabio Caccioli, Giacomo Livan, Guido Montagna, Oreste Nicrosini
arxiv-2401-15968.description: Abstract Participants in socio-economic systems are often ranked based on their performance. Rankings conveniently reduce the complexity of such systems to ordered lists. Yet, it has been shown in many contexts that those who reach the top are not necessarily the most talented, as chance plays a role in shaping rankings.

arxiv-2406-06714.title: Coprocessor Actor Critic: A Model-Based Reinforcement Learning Approach For Adaptive Brain Stimulation
arxiv-2406-06714.creator: Michelle Pan, Mariah Schrum, Vivek Myers, Erdem Bıyık, Anca Dragan
arxiv-2406-06714.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Michelle Pan, Mariah Schrum, Vivek Myers, Erdem Bıyık, Anca Dragan. Adaptive brain stimulation can treat neurological conditions such as Parkinson’s disease and post-stroke motor deficits by influencing abnormal neural activity. Because of patient heterogeneity, each patient requires a unique stimulation policy to achieve optimal neural responses. Model-free reinforcement learning (MFRL) holds promise in learning effective policies for a variety of similar control tasks, but is limited in domains like brain stimulation by a need for numerous costly environment interactions.

arxiv-2410-22380.title: Discrete Modeling via Boundary Conditional Diffusion Processes
arxiv-2410-22380.creator: Yuxuan Gu, Xiaocheng Feng, Lei Huang, Yingsheng Wu, Zekun Zhou, Weihong Zhong, Kun Zhu, Bing Qin
arxiv-2410-22380.description: Abstract We present an novel framework for efficiently and effectively extending the powerful continuous diffusion processes to discrete modeling. Previous approaches have suffered from the discrepancy between discrete data and continuous modeling. Our study reveals that the absence of guidance from discrete boundaries in learning probability contours is one of the main reasons.

arxiv-2504-20407.title: Discovery of a variable yellow supergiant progenitor for the Type IIb SN 2024abfo
arxiv-2504-20407.creator: Zexi Niu(牛泽茜), Ning-Chen Sun, Justyn R. Maund, Zhen Guo, Wenxiong Li, Meng Sun(孙萌), Jifeng Liu
arxiv-2504-20407.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zexi Niu(牛泽茜), Ning-Chen Sun, Justyn R. Maund, Zhen Guo, Wenxiong Li, Meng Sun(孙萌), Jifeng Liu. We report the discovery of a progenitor candidate for the Type IIb SN 2024abfo using multi-epoch pre-explosion images from the Hubble Space Telescope and the Dark Energy Camera Legacy Survey . The progenitor exhibited a ∼ \sim 0.7-mag decline in F814W from 2001 to 2013, followed by significant brightening and color fluctuations in the g g , r r and z z bands.

arxiv-2510-09870.title: Probing the Physics of Dusty Outflows through Complex Organic Molecules in the Early Universe
arxiv-2510-09870.creator: Andrey Vayner, Tanio Díaz-Santos, Carl D. Ferkinhoff, Peter R. M. Eisenhardt, Daniel Stern, Lee Armus, Brandon S. Hensley, Daniel Anglés-Alcázar, Roberto J. Assef, Román Fernández Aranda, Andrew W. Blain, Hyunsung D. Jun, Norman W. Murray, Shelley Wright, Chao-Wei Tsai, Thomas Lai, Niranjan Chandra
arxiv-2510-09870.description: Abstract Galaxy-scale outflows are of critical importance for galaxy formation and evolution. Dust grains are the main sites for the formation of molecules needed for star formation but are also important for the acceleration of outflows that can remove the gas reservoir critical for stellar mass growth.

arxiv-2511-15463.title: How To Cook The Fragmented Rug Pull?
arxiv-2511-15463.creator: Minh Trung Tran, Nasrin Sohrabi, Zahir Tari, Qin Wang
arxiv-2511-15463.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Minh Trung Tran, Nasrin Sohrabi, Zahir Tari, Qin Wang. Existing rug pull detectors assume a simple workflow: the deployer keeps liquidity pool (LP) tokens and performs one or a few large sells (within a day) that collapse the pool and cash out. In practice, however, many real-world exits violate these assumptions by splitting the attack across both time and actor dimensions: attackers break total extraction into many low-impact trades and route proceeds through multiple non-owner addresses, producing low-visibility drains.

arxiv-2512-09708.title: A simple geometric proof for the characterisation of e-merging functions
arxiv-2512-09708.creator: Eugenio Clerico
arxiv-2512-09708.description: Abstract E-values offer a powerful framework for aggregating evidence across different (possibly dependent) statistical experiments. A fundamental question is to identify e-merging functions, namely mappings that merge several e-values into a single valid e-value. A simple and elegant characterisation of this function class was recently obtained by 6 , though via technically involved arguments.

arxiv-2601-17407.title: Efficient Dilated Squeeze and Excitation Neural Operator for Differential Equations
arxiv-2601-17407.creator: Prajwal Chauhan pc3377@nyu.edu, Salah Eddine Choutri sc8101@nyu.edu, Saif Eddin Jabari sej7@nyu.edu
arxiv-2601-17407.description: Abstract Fast and accurate surrogates for physics-driven partial differential equations (PDEs) are essential in fields such as aerodynamics, porous media design, and flow control. However, many transformer-based models and existing neural operators remain parameter-heavy, resulting in costly training and sluggish deployment.

arxiv-2602-08787.title: Accessibility and Serviceability Assessment to Inform Offshore Wind Energy Development and Operations off the U.S. East Coast Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2602-08787.creator: Cory Petersen, Feng Ye, Jiaxiang Ji, Josh Kohut, Ahmed Aziz Ezzat ∗, David Saginaw, Avril Montanti, Jack Cammarota
arxiv-2602-08787.description: Abstract The economic success of offshore wind energy projects relies on accurate projections of the construction, and operations and maintenance (O&M) costs. These projections must consider the logistical complexities introduced by adverse met-ocean conditions that can prohibit access to the offshore assets for sustained periods of time.

arxiv-2605-21561.creator: Mathieu Cherpitel, Thomas Bäck, Martijn R. Tannemaat, Anna V. Kononova, [0.8em] LIACS, Leiden University, Leiden, The Netherlands

pmc-10497596.title: Improved patient mortality predictions in emergency departments with deep learning data-synthesis and ensemble models
pmc-10497596.creator: Byounghoon Son, Jinwoo Myung, Younghwan Shin, Sangdo Kim, Sung Hyun Kim, Jong-Moon Chung, Jiyoung Noh, Junho Cho, Hyun Soo Chung
pmc-10497596.description: The triage process in emergency departments (EDs) relies on the subjective assessment of medical practitioners, making it unreliable in certain aspects. There is a need for a more accurate and objective algorithm to determine the urgency of patients. This paper explores the application of advanced data-synthesis algorithms, machine learning (ML) algorithms, and ensemble models to predict patient mortality.

pmc-10560849.title: Precision in treatment evaluation: importance of minimal clinically important differences (MCIDs) of outcome measures for autoimmune blistering diseases
pmc-10560849.creator: Henry Tseng, Corey Stone, Dédée F. Murrell
pmc-10560849.description: Autoimmune blistering diseases (AIBDs) comprise a group of rare conditions marked by autoantibodies that specifically target intercellular adhesion molecules. Despite the progress made in comprehending the disease and the increasing number of treatment options available, there is still no definitive cure for AIBDs such as pemphigus, and it continues to have a devastating impact on those affected.

pmc-10636087.title: Prevalence and identification of caprine pasteurellosis in pneumonic goats in Bangladesh
pmc-10636087.creator: Md Habibur Rahman, Sonia Akther, Md Shahin Alam, Md Zakir Hassan, Md Samun Sarker, Md Zulfekar Ali, Md Giasuddin, Sadek Ahmed
pmc-10636087.description: Objective:This research aimed to assess the prevalence of caprine pasteurellosis, isolate and identify pasteurellosis (Mannheimia haemolytica and Pasteurella multocida) in pneumonic goats, and discover the main bacterial cause of pneumonia.Materials and Methods:One hundred and five samples (94 nasal swabs and 11 lung tissues) from goats suspected of having pneumonia were taken and transferred aseptically to the laboratory.

pmc-11494394.title: TRIM55 Aggravates Cardiomyocyte Apoptosis After Myocardial Infarction via Modulation of the Nrf2/HO-1 Pathway
pmc-11494394.creator: Yuxin Bu, Yanxia Liu, Meili Liu, Chenghui Yan, Jing Wang, Hanlin Wu, Haixu Song, Dali Zhang, Kai Xu, Dan Liu, Yaling Han
pmc-11494394.description: Visual Abstract Myocardial infarction (MI) is a major public health problem with a high global prevalence and mortality rate.1,2 MI-related heart failure remains a major problem without targeted therapy. Many factors, such as loss of cardiomyocytes, inflammation, and myocardial fibrosis, are associated with MI progression. Cardiomyocyte loss is the primary cause of MI-induced cardiac injury and dysfunction caused by MI.

pmc-12501279.title: Large language models for autism: evaluating theory of mind tasks in a gamified environment
pmc-12501279.creator: Christian Poglitsch, Anna Reiss, Selina C Wriessnegger, Johanna Pirker
pmc-12501279.description: Autism Spectrum Disorder often significantly affects reciprocal social communication, leading to difficulties in interpreting social cues, recognizing emotions, and maintaining verbal interactions. These challenges can make everyday conversations especially demanding. To support autistic people in developing their social competence and communication abilities, we propose an interactive game specifically designed to enhance social understanding.

pmc-12582083.title: Design strategy primer for organ-on-chips
pmc-12582083.creator: Ting Cao, Peicheng Xu, Chen Yang, Yu Chen, Yongcheng Wang, Jiayu Zhang, Fangfu Ye
pmc-12582083.description: Organ-on-a-chip (OoC) has emerged as a revolutionary technique in recent decades, capable of replicating essential aspects of physiological and pathophysiological processes of human organs in vitro. Serving as an effective tissue culture method for creating digital twins, OoCs show significant promise and have found applications in disease modelling, drug screening, and tissue engineering.

pmc-12757753.title: Exploratory analysis of nutrient composition of adult and senior dog diets
pmc-12757753.creator: Kyle German, Cynthia Melgoza, Camille Torres-Henderson
pmc-12757753.description: IntroductionSenior dog foods are often marketed as distinct from adult formulations, yet no specific nutrient profiles exist for this life stage. This study evaluated nutrient composition of over-the-counter adult and senior canine diets in relation to Association of American Feed Control Officials (AAFCO) adult maintenance requirements.

pmc-12838504.title: Preservation of eGFRcre for 1 year with HIF-PHI in non-dialysis patients: a retrospective observational cohort study
pmc-12838504.creator: Tomohiro Aigami, Tomoyuki Ishigo, Mai Miyao, Masatoshi Nonoyama, Tomohisa Yamashita, Masayuki Koyama, Satoshi Fujii, Toshiyuki Yano, Masato Furuhashi, Masahide Fukudo, Takaki Toda
pmc-12838504.description: BackgroundHypoxia-inducible factor prolyl hydroxylase inhibitors (HIF-PHIs) effectively increase hemoglobin levels to treat anemia in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, there is a paucity of studies on the effect of HIF-PHIs on renal outcomes, such as estimated glomerular filtration rate based on serum creatinine (eGFRcre).

pmc-12980496.title: Bead-Ejection Scenario in Electrospray Ionization of Multidomain Nucleic Acids
pmc-12980496.creator: Debasmita Ghosh, Frédéric Rosu, Valérie Gabelica
pmc-12980496.description: Understanding how biomolecules acquire their charge and retain their solution conformation during electrospray ionization (ESI) is crucial for native mass spectrometry (native MS) interpretation. Here, we examine the charging and gas phase conformation of nucleic acid constructs comprising folded G-quadruplex “beads” linked by unstructured polythymine regions.

pmc-13155279.title: Superior Impact‐Resistant Composite Hydrogels Through an Ionic Coupling Strategy
pmc-13155279.creator: Hao Zhuo, Quyang Liu, Xinyu Dong, Hongzhi Zheng, Lingyi Hong, Wei Zhai
pmc-13155279.description: Impact resistance emerges from the coupling of strong load‐bearing networks and dynamic interfacial interactions that enable effective stress transfer and energy dissipation. Although hydrogels are promising candidates for impact‐resistant soft materials, it remains challenging to reinforce both networks and interfaces simultaneously in hydrogels, which limits their performance under high strain‐rate loading.

pmc-13194063.title: Editorial: Overcoming (in)visible barriers: gender, work and discrimination
pmc-13194063.creator: Yvonne Ehrstein, Stefano Maiani, Cláudia Andrade
pmc-13194063.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ten invisible yet systemic mechanisms embedded within everyday workplace interactions and gendered organizational structures (Acker, 1990; Jones et al., 2017). In recent years, campaigns such as #MeToo have amplified both the visibility of gender discrimination in organizations and the role of social media in enabling collective action against workplace discrimination and inequality; a development that may also have contributed to the intensifying shift from blatant to more subtle forms of discrimination (Dipboye and Halverson, 2004; Quan-Haase et al., 2021).

pmc-13413696.title: Differential Surgery on the Rheumatoid Wrist: Patient Satisfaction and Clinical Outcome
pmc-13413696.creator: Christoph Biehl, Madita Biehl, Lotta Biehl
pmc-13413696.description: Background and Objectives: The wrist is one of the most common sites of rheumatic disease. Based on the graded deformities of Larsen et al., surgery has been adapted to minimize harm while maximizing benefit to the individual. This study aims to survey the institutional experience, describing functional outcomes and patient satisfaction across several surgical approaches, without formal statistical comparison.

pmc-13444223.title: Molecular phylogeny and morphology reveal two new species and one new record of Ophiocordyceps (Ophiocordycipitaceae, Hypocreales) parasitic on Hymenoptera in China
pmc-13444223.creator: Ze-Mei Chen, He-Fa Liao, Fang-Wei Lou, Rui Hu, Jin-Long Jia, Wen-Bo Zeng, Zhu-Liang Yang, Ai-Li Zhang, Yuan-Bing Wang

pmc-13483864.title: Hematological consequences of environmental change during dewilding of rhesus macaques
pmc-13483864.creator: Annabelle Smith, Kasalina Kiwanuka, Gabriela Pessenda, Andrew R. Rahmberg, Jacob K. Flynn, Richard Herbert, Jason M. Brenchley, P’ng Loke
pmc-13483864.description: The environment shapes immune system development and the regulation of inflammatory responses, however the hematological consequences of a major environmental change, such as those experienced during migration, remain poorly understood. Here, we assess the immunological consequences in male rhesus macaques as they transitioned from an outdoor provisioned environment to an indoor laboratory facility in a process we term ‘dewilding.
